title: Momentum analysis: put it together
target: Use a model to compare a deflection option and its limits.
criteria: Compute the required change before evaluating an option.
Keep impulse, velocity change and displacement distinct.
Communicate assumptions with the numerical result.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A 300 kg target needs a 9 m sideways offset after 60 s of ideal drift. What added sideways velocity is required?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 300 kg target needs Δv = 0.15 m/s. What impulse is required?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Which set correctly distinguishes the quantities?
options: All three have units of m/s.
Impulse: m; velocity change: N; offset: kg.
Impulse: N·s; velocity change: m/s; offset: m.
cpa.guide: J changes momentum; Δv describes motion change; Δx is displacement.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A 6 N·s impulse acts on a 120 kg target, followed by 80 s of ideal drift. What offset results?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Which statement properly reports an ideal drift prediction?
options: An 8 m offset, assuming the added sideways velocity remains constant.
An 8 N offset because impulse is a distance.
8 m/s of displacement with no stated model.
Exactly 8 m in every possible orbit.
cpa.guide: A useful result includes units and the assumptions supporting it.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A proposal halves delivered impulse but doubles lead time for the same target. In the constant-drift model, compare offsets.
cpa.guide: Δx = (J/M)t; halving J and doubling t cancel.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
